job.style: a description of a classroom activity or experiment and what it shows

response.passage: In our science lab today, we investigated the quality of water and air. We first examined a sample of clear, sparkling water from a local stream. Although it looked perfectly clean, our chemical test strips revealed high levels of dissolved pesticides and lead, proving that clear water can still contain invisible, dangerous toxins. We then discussed how to make water safe. We learned that while boiling kills germs, it cannot remove dissolved chemical pollutants. Next, we looked at the atmosphere. We discussed how the greenhouse effect is actually a natural process that keeps our planet warm enough for life. Without these gases, Earth would be too cold to inhabit. However, human activities are increasing these gases, leading to global warming. Finally, we analyzed air quality. We observed that even when air looks invisible and has no smell, it can contain harmful microscopic particles. We also clarified that smog is not just natural fog; it is a dangerous mixture of smoke and fog caused by industrial emissions and vehicle exhaust. Understanding these differences helps us realize that our senses are not enough to detect pollution, and that natural processes are often distorted by human actions.
response.summary: This activity demonstrates that water and air can be polluted even when they appear clean. It also clarifies that natural processes like the greenhouse effect are essential, while human-made smog and chemical contaminants pose serious risks.
